environmental.storage-temp-datasheet: -40 to 70 C (-40 to 158 F), per the data sheet

features.encryption: none on the DR3A-54; all ports (MACsec and TunnelSec) on the DR3AM-54 and DR3AK-54
features.optics-osfp: datasheet: the two OSFP-LS (line-system) ports are "for dense 400G-ZR deployment", and "Arista's R3A platforms are optimized to support high power 400ZR OSFP and QSFP-DD optical modules".
features.optics-qsfp-dd: datasheet: each QSFP-DD port runs 400G, or 200G, 100G, 50G, 40G (QSFP+) and 25/10G modes by breakout. Maximum values are uni-dimensional and may need breakout cables or transceivers.
features.osfp-ls: 2 x OSFP-LS ports for dense 400G-ZR deployment
features.precision-timing: PTP and SyncE with OCXO and PPS/10M/ToD inputs

management.console: RJ-45 serial (RS-232), 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, no flow control

physical.size-over-ears: 48.3 x 8.8 x 76.4 cm (19 x 3.50 x 30.1 inches) per Table 1 of the guide, which includes the rack ears. The data sheet gives 43.99 x 8.79 x 76.39 cm "inc. handles".
physical.weight-note: 27.9 kg (61.6 lbs) per Table 1 of the guide; "61.6 lbs (27.94 kg)" per the data sheet

platform.software: EOS; minimum release 4.29.1 per the data sheet

power.power-draw-note: Table 4 of the guide: "933 W / 1715 W" for the DR3A-54, DR3AM-54 and DR3AK-54. The data sheet measures the typical at 25 C ambient with 50 percent load on all ports, excluding transceivers.

configs.name: ac

configs.description: The DR3AK-54 with large routes and TunnelSec: DCS-7280DR3AK-54-F, the same face, supplies and fans as the base switch. Table 4 gives it the base switch's power draw. Its face prints "7280DR3AK-54" on the model plate, as figure C-1 does.
configs.name: ac-k

configs.description: The DR3AM-54 with TunnelSec: DCS-7280DR3AM-54-F, the same face, supplies and fans as the base switch. Table 4 gives it the base switch's power draw.
configs.name: ac-m

configs.description: The chassis as it ships: two AC supplies and four fans in, all fifty-four QSFP-DD and both OSFP cages empty. The orderable builds below are this chassis with a licence and encryption variant.
configs.name: base

configs.description: Two DC supplies in place of the AC ones, front-to-rear air: what a "DCS-7280DR3A-54#" order (configurable fans and psu) with PWR-3001-DC-RED gives. The data sheet lists no DC part number of its own, so this is a worked build and not an orderable one.
configs.name: dc

gaps.wanted: A FIGURE OF THE DR3A-54 AND THE DR3AM-54 FRONT. Figure C-1 is captioned for all three models but prints the plate "7280DR3AK-54", so it is a picture of the DR3AK-54. The model plate of the other two is not shown. The `ac-k` face prints the figure's "7280DR3AK-54"; the base switch's plate reads "7280DR3A-54", and on `ac-m` that line is a stand-in for the M plate. A photograph of each plate closes the base and M ones.

WHICH WAY EACH UPRIGHT CAGE FACES. The cages stand on end and are turned 90; whether the bail is at the right or the left, and whether the three in a column are built alike, is not resolved in a 127 ppi figure. A photograph or a drawing of the faceplate that shows a cage lip closes it.

THE WHITE NUMBER TABS OVER THE CAGES. Figure C-1 draws a white square with a large numeral over the centre of each cage. A seated cage hides what is painted under it and the library has no layer above a cage for printed matter, so the numbers are modelled as the strip legends only. A drawing that says whether the tab is a sticker on the cage or part of it closes it.

THE SYMBOLS OVER THE SYSTEM AND FAN LAMPS, and the small symbols at the left of the console, USB and management jacks. They are printed in blue at about two pixels' height and are not legible in the figure; PS1 and PS2 are. Guide figures A-1 and A-2 say the lamps are labelled in one of two ways and the held figure does not say which this chassis uses.
A BLUE SYMBOL (a circle with a mark in it) ABOVE THE ToD CONNECTOR, at about 12.0 mm from the left and 7.5 mm down. Figure C-1 draws it and no callout or table names it. It is not modelled.

WHETHER THE PPS AND 10MHZ JACKS ARE SMB OR SMA. The guide calls them "E-Sync clock connectors" and the data sheet "PPS/10M/ToD inputs"; neither names the connector. They are seated as std/smb@1 from their drawn size and their direction (input or output) is not stated either.

WHAT THE ToD CONNECTOR IS. Figure C-1 draws a vertical slot with a jack screw at each end, which reads as a locking D-shaped connector; the data sheet's accessory "CAB-SYNCE-RJ" names a USB-C mate. It is seated as std/usb-c@1 with its screws drawn as decor, as the 7280DR3A-36 does.

THE USB GENERATION. The guide says "USB port" and the data sheet "USB Ports 1"; neither gives a generation, and figure C-1 draws a black tongue. The port is seated with the `usb2` (white) skin as the one that claims least; a data sheet line giving the generation closes it.

A BLACK ROUND HOLE at the left edge, 1.9 mm from it and 43.8 mm down, under the clock jacks. Figure C-1 draws it and nothing names it (an ESD socket is a candidate on other switches). It is drawn as a hole in decor and carries no part.
THE THIN BANDS OF HONEYCOMB above and below the strips. They are 2.6 mm tall, under one cell of the library's tile, and are not drawn; the fields between the columns are.
THE PRINTING AT THE REAR. The guide's rear panel figure is 1.19 px/mm and its labels are unreadable. The supplies and fans print no numbers that resolve. A rear photograph closes it.

THE PWR-3001-DC FACE. The guide shows the PWR-1900-DC and PWR-500-DC (figure 4-5) and no PWR-3001-DC. Table 7 note 2 says its terminals are "twin #10 studs spaced for dual-hole lug with 5/8 inch hole spacing"; the supply here is the AC housing with a plain two-pole block, and the protective earth terminal "on the opposite side" is not drawn. The data sheet reads "AWG #3 Max" for the DC input connector and table 7 reads 1 to 2 AWG; the larger conductor (the guide's) is the one a lug takes.

THE SIDE GROUNDING POINT. Table 6 and section 4.2 of the guide put the DR3A-54's grounding point on the side of the chassis, taking the KIT-GND-EXT-2RU extender (the data sheet: "DR3A-54 Only"), and figure 4-3 draws the kit on another switch from an angle. No document gives the point's position or the kit's size, so neither side face carries it and the kit is not modelled.

THE KITS, AND THE EAR POSITION THAT IS NOT FLUSH. `chassis.ears` states the one position the guide names for a 2RU switch: section 3.5 says the bracket sits "either flush with the front and rear panels, or not flush with the panels", and section 3.4 gives no two-post mounting for the 2RU switches, so the position is `4-post` only. It has no `at` (the guide's mounting figures are isometric drawings of other switches, the 7050 and the 7050SX-128), no `default` (no figure shows the ears as shipped) and the "not flush" case is left out because the guide does not say which way it sits. The data sheet's ordering information lists KIT-7203 (spare tool-free accessory kit v2 for 2RU, 4-post mount, 2x SAF-D-C20) and KIT-7004-2UL (extended tool-free 4-post kit for 2-4RU) for the DR3A-54. No document dimensions the parts of either, and none gives KIT-7004-2UL a range or a parts list. A kit contract needs its parts as components with a size, so neither kit is modelled and `chassis.kits` is left out.
THE POWER DRAW OF FAN-7012H. Neither the guide nor the data sheet gives it. The supplies' own output (3000 W) is stated and is written.
The M variant prints its own model line on the plate. The K plate is drawn from figure C-1; the M plate has no figure, so `ac-m` prints the base line.

configurations.note: THREE ORDERABLE CONFIGURATIONS OF ONE FACE. The data sheet's ordering information for the 7280DR3A-54 lists DCS-7280DR3A-54-F ("front to rear air, 2 x AC"), DCS-7280DR3AM-54-F ("TunnelSec") and DCS-7280DR3AK-54-F ("large routes and TunnelSec"), and the same three ending "#" ("configurable fans and psu"). The F orders are the only part numbers with a fixed build, so they are the orderable configurations. The "#" orders take their supplies and fans to order, which is how a DC build is bought (PWR-3001-DC-RED is a listed spare and table 4 lists PWR-3001-DC); there is no DC part number, so the DC build is a `kind: example` configuration, shown but not exported. The data sheet lists no secure-boot (S) variant of the 54, as it does for the DR3AK-36. Table 4 of the guide gives one figure (933 W typical, 1715 W maximum) for the DR3A-54, DR3AM-54 and DR3AK-54, so no configuration states a power of its own. The guide's Table 1 gives all three one size and weight; the data sheet's model comparison table differs only in the Encryption row (none, all ports, all ports).

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, 0 to 3,000 m, 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. The data sheet's environmental table gives the same operating and altitude figures and humidity, and a storage range of -40 to 70 C. The guide (the newer, 2025-05-16 against 2025-04-15) is used for storage; the data sheet's is in `other` as written.

field-replaceable-units.note: EVERY FAN MODULE AND POWER SUPPLY IS A BAY. The guide's appendix E: "All fans and power supplies are hot swappable" and "all slots must be filled or covered with a blank for operation". The data sheet's comparison table: "Hot-swap Power Supplies 2 (1+1 redundant)", "Hot-swappable Fans 4 (N+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7012H" and "Power Supplies PWR-3001 (AC or DC)". Nothing in the held documents draws a blank for either bay, so none is modelled. The supply and fan the DR3A-54 takes are front-to-rear (red) only: the data sheet lists "Airflow Direction: Front to Rear" and only the RED spares (PWR-3001-AC-RED, PWR-3001-DC-RED, FAN-7012H-RED). The guide's section 2.1 says a red handle is an air-exit module and a blue one an air-inlet module, so this switch is wholly red and has no airflow configuration.

gate-1.note: Figure C-1 is a 856 x 349 px raster (PDF image, 127 ppi). The chassis in it spans 825 px (x 2 to 827) and 164.5 px (y 105 to 269.5): aspect 5.01, against 5.005 for the data sheet's 43.99 x 8.79 cm body (0.2 percent out), so the figure shows the body with no ears and PASSES Gate 1. Scale 1.874 px/mm on x and 1.871 on y; 1.874 is used for both, so one pixel is 0.53 mm. Every front position below is a reading good to about one pixel and is estimated. The rear figure D-4 is a 571 x 153 px raster whose chassis is 527 px (x 0 to 527) by 105 px (y 47 to 152): the same chassis frame as figure D-3 of the 7280DR3A-36, at 1.193 px/mm, with the red fan frames at the same pixels (x 9, 126, 228 and 330, 96 px wide, y 52 to 150).

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-sale notice for the 7280DR3A-54 (2026-10-22, a web search for "Arista 7280DR3A-54 end of sale announcement"): none found for this family. The notices that exist are for other 7280 models (the DCS-7280CR3K-36S, advisory 23790, and the older 7280QR-C36 and QR-C72), so the field reads none-announced.

line-system-ports.note: TWO OSFP CAGES stacked at the lower right, "Line system port (OSFP)" (callout 10 of the figure) and "2 x OSFP-LS ports for dense 400G-ZR deployment" in the data sheet, standing upright like the QSFP-DD cages and printed 55 (upper) and 56 (lower) beside a green strip. The pair measures 28 px (14.9 mm) wide and 86.6 px (46.2 mm) tall at x 787 to 815 px and y 174 to 261 px, which is two std/osfp@1 (23.1 x 13.5 mm) turned a quarter, touching: centres 426.4 mm from the left and 48.4 and 71.7 mm down. A green strip 2.3 mm wide at their right (x 433.8, y 36.9 to 83.1 mm) prints "55", LINE (turned) and "56"; a small lamp sits on it opposite each cage. The two cages are stacked down a column and are not a belly-to-belly pair (see stack-orientation).

management-ports.note: A STACK OF THREE at the upper right, one over another, in a black well 17.4 x 33.0 mm at x 416.7 mm: the Ethernet management port (callout 3, RJ-45 with its two lamps drawn in the top corners) at the top, the USB port (callout 4, Type A, horizontal) in the middle and the serial console (callout 5, RJ-45) at the bottom, the console below the USB port. The callout arrows point at the upper jack's top-left lamp, at the USB slot and at the lower jack. The guide's section 4.5 lists the cables: RJ-45 to DB-9 serial adapter and an RJ-45 Ethernet cable; the data sheet gives "RS-232 Serial Ports 1 (RJ-45)", "USB Ports 1" and "100/1000 Mgmt Ports 1" (as printed). The management jack is taken as 10/100/1000 (guide section 4.5: "Connect to 10/100/1000 management network") and so `1g`, where the data sheet's line reads "100/1000". Jack centres 425.2 mm from the left and 10.4, 19.6 and 28.8 mm down; the library's jack is 15.8 mm wide where the figure's measures about 13.3.

nameplate.note: A light plate at the upper left, 15.0 x 43.9 mm, carries the maker's wordmark, turned to read upward, beside the ToD connector and the clock jacks, and a narrow plate at the lower left (5.4 x 24.4 mm) carries the model line turned to read upward. The wordmark is not drawn; its box is the `logo-zone` region. The model line is plain text and is drawn by the label component `arista/7280dr3a-model-plate`: figure C-1 prints "7280DR3AK-54" because it is a picture of the DR3AK-54, the encryption variant of this chassis, and the guide's one figure serves the DR3A-54, the DR3AK-54 and the DR3AM-54. The `ac-k` configuration places the `k` skin, which prints that line. The other configurations place the default skin, which reads 7280DR3A-54, the plate of the device this file is named for. The M plate is not shown in the guide, so on `ac-m` the default line is a stand-in (see gaps).

numbering.note: THE NUMBERS ARE PRINTED TWICE ON THE FIGURE and the model follows the strips. A white box with a large numeral sits over each cage in figure C-1, and the orange strips print the same numbers small: the top strip of a column prints `N-up-arrow` at its left and `down-arrow N+1` at its right (1 and 2, 4 and 5, 7 and 8, 10 and 11, ... 52 and 53), and the bottom strip prints `N+2-up-arrow` (3, 6, 9, 12, ... 54). The numeral boxes were read on a five-times enlargement of columns one to five, and the strip text on a ten-times one of column one. A seated cage hides anything painted under it, so the model prints the strip legends (which show in every render) and not the boxes. The numbers run down each column: port n is in column ceil(n/3), and its row is (n - 1) mod 3, the top when n is 1 mod 3. Callout 11 of the figure, "Port numbers", covers both prints. Numbering starts at 1. Interface names (Ethernet1 to Ethernet54 and their breakouts) are EOS names and are not printed on the metal; they are not modelled.

port-lamps.note: ONE LAMP PER PORT, three to a column, in the grey bands between the cages: the band between the first and second cage holds two triangles, an up-pointing one 1.9 mm left of the column centre (the first port's) and a down-pointing one 1.9 mm right of it (the second port's), and the band between the second and third holds one down-pointing triangle at the right (the third port's); y 31.4 and 56.4 mm from the top (figure C-1, five-times enlargement of columns one to five). The guide's Appendix A.1.2 says port LEDs are "located in the vicinity of their corresponding ports" and table 10 gives the states: off link down, green link up, yellow software-disabled, flashing yellow failed diagnostics. The lamps are triangles (the arrows point to the cage they serve) and are drawn with common/led-arrow-sm.

port-wall.note: FIFTY-FOUR QSFP-DD CAGES IN EIGHTEEN COLUMNS OF THREE, EACH STANDING UPRIGHT. The orange strips of figure C-1 were found as connected components: the top strips start at x 37, 79, 120, 162, 203, 245, 286, 328, 370, 411, 453, 494, 536, 577, 618, 660, 701 and 743 px, a pitch of 41.53 px = 22.16 mm, each 20.5 px (10.9 mm) wide, centred 24.2 mm from the left for column one. The cages in a column are 19.5 mm tall bezels (121.5 to 158, 168.5 to 205, 215.5 to 252.5 px) on a 47 px = 25.1 mm pitch, centred 18.6, 43.7 and 68.8 mm below the top; a cage is 19 mm long and 10 mm wide in the registry (std/qsfp-dd@1, 19.0 x 10.0), so each is turned a quarter and stands 10 wide and 19 tall. The figure draws the bezel about 10.9 wide, which is the strip's width. An orange strip lies above each column (y 114 to 120.5 px, 4.8 to 8.2 mm) and another below it (y 254 to 260.5 px, 79.5 to 83.0 mm); a grey band holds the lamps between the cages.

rear-layout.note: FIGURE D-4, the rear with a plain separation between fans 1 and 2 and no ground, 2RU: four fan modules left of the middle and two power supplies stacked at the right. The guide draws four generic rear panels (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. D-1 and D-2 are 1RU. Of the 2RU pair, D-3 has an "Earth grounding pad" (callout 7) and D-4 has a plain separation between fans 1 and 2 with no ground. Table 6 of the guide says the DR3A-54 grounds with the KIT-GND-EXT-2RU kit on the SIDE of the chassis ("the grounding point is on the side of the chassis for the switches that support the KIT-GND-EXT-2RU grounding kit") where the DR3A-36 attaches directly at the rear, so the DR3A-54 is mapped to D-4. THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED: it follows from fan count (four), height (2RU), supply count (two) and table 6, not from a caption. The data sheet's ordering information lists "KIT-GND-EXT-2RU ... (DR3A-54 Only)". MEASURED at 1.193 px/mm on the red fan frames (the same pixels as figure D-3): four modules 79.6 wide on 98.0, 85.5 and 85.5 mm steps (the first step spans the separation), x 5.9, 103.9, 189.4 and 274.9; supplies at x 361 (73.5 wide), top at 2.0 and 45.0 mm.

separation.note: A plain grey strip 15.0 mm wide between fans 1 and 2 (x 87.2 to 102.2), as figure D-4 draws it: no holes, no symbol. Where the 7280DR3A-36 has a grounding pad, this chassis has none on the rear: its grounding point is the side kit of table 6.

size-conflict.note: The guide's Table 1 gives 48.3 x 8.8 x 76.4 cm and the data sheet "43.99 x 8.79 x 76.39 cm inc. handles". The first includes the rack ears (19 inch), the second is the body: the body is modelled (width 440.0, height 87.9, depth 763.9), as the library does for every rack device, and the figure's aspect (Gate 1) agrees with the body.

sources.note: 7280R3A Series Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, DOC-07042-01, 59 pages, PDF created 2025-05-16 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280R3A.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage environment), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), Table 6 (grounding of the 2RU switches), section 2.1 (airflow orientation), sections 4.4 and 4.5 (power and serial cables), Appendix A (status indicators, figures A-1 and A-2, tables 9 to 13), Appendix C (front panel, figure C-1: DCS-7280DR3A-54, DCS-7280DR3AK-54 and DCS-7280DR3AM-54), Appendix D (rear panels, figures D-1 to D-4) and Appendix E (power supplies and fan modules, "all fans and power supplies are hot swappable"). 7280R3A Series Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 04-0040-26, 27 pages, dated April 15th, 2025 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7280R3A-Datasheet.pdf): the 7280DR3A-54 model comparison table, power supply specifications, ordering information and the platform overview. Held intake files read first: SOURCES.md, COVERAGE.md and the stencil folder. No 3D model, no CAD drawing, no studio photograph and no Visio stencil is held (the stencil zip could not be fetched), and the data sheet's only picture of the face is a small thumbnail, so figure C-1 is the instrument.

stack-orientation.note: Every cage is turned 90 (its bail to the right). The library's convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S3) pairs a column of cages turned 270 and 90 whose bellies face each other ACROSS the stack, and "never two cages down a column"; here the cages are stacked down a column, three high, and the columns are 22.16 mm apart, so no two cages face each other and no pair exists to be turned. The turn is therefore the library's default for an upright cage turned to stand on its end and not an observation: the figure draws the bezels at 1.874 px/mm and the cage lip and the bail are not resolved, so a photograph of the faceplate overturns it. See the gap for the turn.

status-block.note: FOUR LAMPS at the right of the management block, one over another 5.9 mm apart at x 434.4 mm: system status, fan status, power supply 1 status and power supply 2 status (figure C-1 callouts 6 to 9; guide Appendix A.1.1, figures A-1 and A-2: "labeled either as in Figure A-1 or as in Figure A-2"). The two lower lamps are printed PS1 and PS2 at their right; the two upper lamps carry a symbol (a circle with a mark, a fan) instead of a word. The symbols are not drawn: their strokes are two pixels wide and resolve to a blob (see gaps). States are table 9's: the system lamp blinking green (powering up), green, blue (beacon) or amber; the fan lamp green, amber or red; the supply lamps green or off.

timing.note: ToD AND TWO CLOCK CONNECTORS in the strip at the left edge (callouts 1 and 2). The ToD connector is a vertical slot 8.3 mm tall with a screw at each end (x 8.3 mm, y 14.4 to 22.7 mm, screws at 11.5 and 25.1 mm); the data sheet's accessory "CAB-SYNCE-RJ  Spare Time of Day adapter cable (USB-C to 2 x RJ-45)" says its mate is USB-C, so std/usb-c@1 is turned a quarter, as the 7280DR3A-36 does. Under it are two gold coax jacks at x 8.3 mm and y 32.2 and 40.2 mm (4.8 mm across), printed PPS (upper) and 10MHz (lower) and turned to read upward. The data sheet's timing line reads "PTP and SyncE with OCXO and PPS/10M/ToD inputs". The coax type is not stated: std/smb@1 is seated because the jacks measure 4.8 mm across, which is the SMB's 4.83 in the registry and not the SMA's 6.35 (see gaps).

vents.note: The figure fills every space not taken by a cage, a strip or a jack with a hexagonal honeycomb: a 11.3 mm field between each pair of columns (seventeen of them, x from 29.6 mm, y 1.8 to 86.0 mm), a black column at the left of column one, a black block under the left plate and a 10 mm field at the right of column eighteen. The library's honeycomb tile is scaled to the figure's cell (about 4.4 mm across flats at the face, read at five times). The thin bands of cells above and below the strips (2.6 mm tall, under one cell) are not drawn.

weight.note: 27.9 kg (61.6 lbs) in the guide's Table 1; the data sheet's comparison table prints "61.6 lbs (27.94 kg)". The same figure to rounding; 27.9 is used.
